[Rating: 6/10] This is a version of Hex which uses a board that splits into smaller spaces in the middle. On your turn you choose any empty space to fill with your color. Your goal is to create an unbroken chain of from one side of the board to the other. I found it interesting, but once you figure out the trick its more like The Game of Nim where the first player can control the game.

[Rating: 6/10] Only played the BGA version.  Do like the fact that the central areas are smaller therefore less absolutely vital.  I dislike the fact that you can basically just plop a handful of outer tiles down and win - I do think you should have to in some way pass through the middle, or at least have some sort of path that touches the central hexes.  Also think that opposite should mean opposite.  Obviously, this may all be the case in the IRL non-BGA adaptation of the game.

[Rating: 6.5/10] PnP  Perfect for when you need something to entertain yourself and another, kind of like tic-tac-toe or dots and boxes or hangman except with a pre-printed board.  There are lots of moves to be made and it can be both strategic and frustrating.

[Rating: 7/10] I don't understand why this clever game is so underrated. It's a good connexion game.
